title: add NVTX ranges, per-operator counters, and microbench instrumentation for runtime profiling
author: Priya Desai
description:
Background:
We need better per-request and per-operator visibility into the serving runtime to diagnose kernel scheduling regressions, KV-cache hot-path overhead, and continuous-batching effects. This PR adds NVTX range annotations around key runtime stages, per-operator counters exposed to Prometheus, and a small microbenchmark harness to exercise batching/scheduling kernels at controlled loads.

What this PR does:
- Adds NVTX ranges for: request_enqueue, batching_window, scheduler_dispatch, kvcache_lookup, kvcache_store, attention_kernel, matmul_kernel, postprocess_step. Ranges are hierarchical and include request id metadata when provided (sampling only).
- Introduces a lightweight per-operator counter API in runtime/telemetry that updates atomic counters for kernel_time_ns, bytes_processed, evictions, cache_hits. Counters are exposed via existing /metrics endpoint with names prefixed redwood_runtime_.
- Microbench tool: tools/microbench/runtime_microbench (C++ + python wrapper) to run synthetic workloads (single-request, burst, sustained) and collect histogram outputs and NVTX-compatible traces (.rdvp). The tool supports parameterized batch sizes and KV-cache hit rates.
- Adds a perf dashboard JSON (observability/grafana/runtime_kernels_dashboard.json) that visualizes kernel durations, queue depth, batch sizes, and KV-cache hit/miss rates.
- Small docs and README for the microbench tool and recommended sampling knobs.

Checklist:
- [x] NVTX ranges added with compile-time flag ENABLE_NVTX (off by default)
- [x] Counters are lock-free/atomic and exported via metrics path
- [x] Microbench binary + python wrapper + quickstart example
- [x] Unit tests for telemetry counters and small integration test for metrics exposition
- [x] Grafana dashboard JSON and dashboard metadata

Testing and CI:
- Unit tests added under runtime/telemetry/test_counters.cc
- Microbench smoke test added to CI matrix (non-flaky mode) that runs microbench with small inputs and asserts output format
- Local profiling validated using nvprof and NVIDIA Nsight to confirm NVTX ranges present in traces

Motivation and impact:
This provides engineers a fast feedback loop when investigating tail-latency regressions related to scheduling and kernel selection. The microbench harness helps reproduce high-throughput scenarios in CI and on perf-canary infra to detect regressions early. NVTX traces make it trivial to correlate GPU-side time with scheduler decisions.

Risk and rollout plan:
- NVTX disabled by default to avoid overhead in production. We will enable sampling and a low-rate collection in canary fleets first.
- Metrics prefixes were chosen to avoid collision with existing names. We will monitor cardinality in canaries for 2 weeks before wider rollout.

Follow-ups:
- Hook microbench results into perf-canary automated regression alerts (ENG-1839).
- Add streaming export of per-request traces to tracing backend when sampling is enabled.

review_comments: Marco Li (2025-11-05): Nice work — NVTX macros look clean. Two asks: 1) please add a compile-time macro to strip metadata payloads to avoid building strings in hot paths; 2) add a unit test that verifies counter increment under concurrent increments.

Priya Desai (2025-11-06): Addressed both asks: added ENABLE_NVTX_METADATA and a test harness test_counters_concurrent that runs 1000 threads incrementing atomics and verifies totals. Pushed new commit b29e1f0.
Dana Kim (2025-11-07): CI failed on windows build because nvtx is not available there. Can we guard with platform macros?
Priya Desai (2025-11-07): Added platform guards and a stub NVTX implementation for non-NVIDIA platforms to make builds deterministic. Updated CMakeLists to conditionally add nvtx sources.
Ethan Park (2025-11-09): Left a minor nits on naming conventions for metrics (suggested redwood_runtime_kernel_time_ms) and asked to document cardinality concerns in the dashboard README.

Priya Desai (2025-11-09): Renamed metrics to suffix _ms where appropriate and added a note in docs/microbench/README.md about cardinality and recommended label cardinality limits. CI now passes. Approving.
merge_commit_message:
add NVTX ranges, per-op counters and microbench instrumentation

This PR adds NVTX annotations, telemetry counters and a microbench tool to exercise runtime kernels. Enables better profiling and perf dashboards.

Closes: ENG-1783, ENG-1839
release_notes: Added runtime NVTX instrumentation (disabled by default) to capture scheduler and kernel boundaries.
Exposed per-operator counters to /metrics with prefix redwood_runtime_.
Added microbench tool to reproduce batching and KV-cache scenarios deterministically.
Included Grafana dashboard for kernel timings and KV-cache metrics.
